name: CRUX (Open-World Evaluations)
description: CRUX (Collaborative Research for Updating AI eXpectations) is a project for systematically conducting open-world evaluations: long-horizon tasks in real-world environments where success cannot be neatly specified or automatically graded. A collaboration of 17 researchers from academia, government, civil society, and industry, CRUX runs new experiments every 1–2 months across AI R&D, governance, and other domains. The first experiment tasked an AI agent with developing and publishing a simple iOS app to the App Store, which involved signing the app, publishing a privacy policy, filling out Apple's review forms, and passing the review process — completed with two errors, one requiring manual intervention.
evaluation_method: human review of task completion in real-world environments; per-experiment qualitative and quantitative reports rather than a single aggregate metric
general_score_metric: per-experiment outcome reports (success/failure plus error analysis); no single aggregate metric across experiments
typical_sota_score: Experiment 1 (iOS app publication): completed with 2 errors, 1 requiring manual intervention
reputation: Recent collaborative initiative (17-author launch); cited by Epoch AI as the canonical example of biting the bullet on hard-to-grade outputs and plugging into pre-existing real-world evaluation practices.
notes: Distinct from CRUXEval (the 800-Python-function code-reasoning benchmark) and from the CRUX RAG context-evaluation framework — both also catalogued in this directory. CRUX (Open-World Evaluations) is a recurring evaluation programme rather than a static dataset; each experiment is a self-contained case study. Aim is to provide empirical evidence about present capabilities and early warnings for capabilities about to become widespread.
